items.title: METR outlines how an assessor could investigate alignment of unreleased AI models
items.summary_en: METR proposes a way for an outside assessor to examine the alignment of unreleased models, drawing on a developer's internal incident records. It is a methodology proposal, not an evaluation result.

items.title: METR outlines how an assessor could investigate control and monitoring of internal AI agents
items.summary_en: METR sets out a proposal for how an assessor could check control and monitoring of AI agents used inside a developer, including whether monitoring coverage is complete. It is a proposal for assessment practice.

items.title: METR proposes better informing the public about loss-of-control risks from frontier AI
items.summary_en: METR proposes a public-disclosure approach for loss-of-control risks from frontier AI development. According to the search summary, access to information would remain at the company's discretion.

items.summary_en: METR describes how it works with AI companies on public-facing risk work, including its past reports. This is an organisational policy and process post.

items.title: METR argues AI agent observability tools are security-critical and shows a proof-of-concept vulnerability
items.summary_en: METR argues that observability tools for AI agents should be treated as security-critical infrastructure. It describes a proof-of-concept vulnerability in an Inspect transcript viewer that could let an agent change what human reviewers see.
items.notes: Not fetched directly (metr.org DNS failure); based on search-tool summary; date from URL slug. Verify before use. Proof of concept only; real-world prevalence not established.
